lines.ruling: Ruling: representation; executable triage 2,430/2,999 agree; 559 candidate-unknown, 10 project-unknown, no value differs (completed: 6 candidate-unknown). Same test (traditional contributions above zero); the reply sums person.ira_trad without its parent person.ira_owner, so it is unknown where the interview never asks the amount. i1040gi p. 95, Line 20.

Ruling: representation; executable triage 2,940/2,999 agree; 40 candidate-unknown, 10 project-unknown, 9 value (completed: 1 value; 2 completed witnesses in total). Every value witness is project true, reply false on a return with no traditional contribution: the reply reads worksheet lines 1a/1b, which are No without a contribution, while the project tests coverage itself. Both readers (ira.lines2to6, ira.cov_gate) also require ira.any_trad, so no value downstream differs. On a separate return both take the spouse's coverage through the same lived-apart rule (i1040gi p. 96, Married persons filing separately).

Ruling: model error; executable triage 2,418/2,999 agree; 559 candidate-unknown, 22 value (completed: 6 candidate-unknown, 6 value). The reply drops the social security condition of the label ('Social security benefits, traditional IRA contributions for 2025, and you or your spouse covered'): it is true on classm.person.2, stage16.ira.i1 and i2 (ssb.any false). The deciding source is the exception of i1040gi p. 31, Lines 6a and 6b, which concerns the benefits worksheet only; a filer with no benefits is not sent to Pub. 590-A by it.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 98, IRA Deduction Worksheet—Continued, Caution, "If married filing jointly and line 10 is less than $14,000 ... stop here and use the worksheet in Pub. 590-A"; i8606 p. 5, Overall Contribution Limit for Traditional and Roth IRAs, "see Kay Bailey Hutchison Spousal IRA Limit in Pub. 590-A for special rules". Both sides test a joint return with line 10 under the caution amount; the project adds 'some traditional or Roth contribution was made' (ira.any_contrib). The two differ only on a return with no IRA contribution, where no line reads the gate: person.ira_line11 is read only with a traditional contribution (person.ira_deduction, person.ira_nondeductible) and person.ira_roth_over only with a Roth contribution. Values agree wherever the gate is read.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 95, Line 20, "If you are filing a joint return and you or your spouse made contributions to both a traditional IRA and a Roth IRA for 2025, don't use the IRA Deduction Worksheet". Both sides take the return-wide reading (amb.2025.ira_both_kinds). The reply reads the amount person.ira_trad, which the interview asks only after person.sav_trad (and person.ira_owner) is Yes; the project reads person.ira_contrib, zero after No. Triage executable-triage-v2 (pass 12f36e046fb1; 1,986 fixtures, 500 generated returns, seed 20261026): 2,585/2,591 agree; the 6 differences are candidate-unknown (the unasked amount, classm.f8880.3, classm.tcw.2), none on a completed return, no value difference.

Ruling: model error; i8606 p. 5, Overall Contribution Limit for Traditional and Roth IRAs, "your limit on contributions to traditional and Roth IRAs is generally the smaller of $7,000 ($8,000 if age 50 or older at the end of 2025) or your taxable compensation". The limit counts Roth contributions with traditional ones; the reply adds only lines 11a and 11b (traditional), so a Roth contribution above the compensation passes (BUG-1154, fixture roth.no_compensation). On returns with traditional contributions only the two agree.

Ruling: representation; equivalent on executable triage, ruled mechanically: the project's line and the reply's agree on every input triage ran (3378 values compared, none different or missing: 2761 on 2761 fixture cases, 500 on 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 117 on 117 partial records; every alternative of the 0 differing choose line(s) reached taken; policy executable-triage-v2). Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 95, Line 20, "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction ... But read the following list before you fill in the worksheet": the special cases matter only with a traditional contribution. The reply drops that condition and folds in its own over_comp (the line 10 caution read without any contribution), its both-kinds test and the deduct-less election. Triage (pass 12f36e046fb1): 1,978/2,591 agree; value records where no traditional contribution was made and the reply refuses through over_comp (classm.f5329.1.deepseek, classm.clcw_next_year.2.deepseek; 7 on completed returns), and candidate-unknown on unasked special-case answers (46 on completed returns). Same reading as the earlier Claude ruling of this line.

Ruling: interface gap and model error; the reply's gate is s8812.combat_pay on every return, the project's is s8812.combat_pay only when a person on the return contributed to a traditional IRA (false otherwise). The reply's note says the request gave it no return-level aggregate of the person collection to make that test: interface gap. Without a traditional IRA contribution there is no IRA deduction to figure, so the combat-pay question cannot change it; on the 2 completed value differences in the recorded witnesses (fixture stage5.return.refund_combat_pay_no_children: combat pay yes, no traditional IRA contribution) the reply's gate is true and the project's false, with no IRA amount on either side. On completed returns where the interview does not ask the combat pay question the reply needs it (candidate-unknown, 71; the recorded witnesses name s8812.combat_pay with the project's value false): a need the source does not have. Triage executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/ira.json`, pass 822691093399; 1,767 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026): 2,152 of 2,336 in-scope comparisons agree; differences by kind {"candidate-unknown": 151, "project-unknown": 10, "value": 23}; the other value differences are on refused (20) or incomplete (1) records. The project line is retained.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 98, worksheet line 12, "Add the amounts on lines 12a and 12b and enter the total on Schedule 1, line 20". No value differs where both sides compute (triage pass 12f36e046fb1: 1,987/2,591 agree), but the reply's line refuses through its special_gate, which has no traditional-contribution condition: candidate-refuses on returns with no IRA contribution (classm.f8889.4.deepseek, classm.f5329.1.deepseek; 7 on completed returns) and 46 candidate-unknown on completed returns from unasked special-case answers. The 1 project refusal (stage16.refuse.ira.over_comp) is the project's cited excess-contribution screen.

Ruling: representation; executable triage 2,329/2,999 agree; 592 candidate-unknown, 68 value, 10 project-unknown (completed: 6 candidate-unknown, 6 value; value pairs all project No, reply Yes). A display line: the project answers line 1a only when the worksheet is used (a traditional contribution); every value witness has none (e.g. classm.person.3, a SIMPLE plan with person.ira_owner false; triage explain of the 6a witnesses shows ira.any_trad false). With a contribution both read the same coverage, including the separate-return rule 'considered covered by a plan unless you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2025' (i1040gi p. 96). Unknowns: the reply reads person.ira_work_plan unasked.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 97, line 1: "Were you covered by a retirement plan (see Were You Covered by a Retirement Plan)?" and "If married filing jointly, was your spouse covered by a retirement plan?"; i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction." Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/ira.json; 1,083 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 57 partial records): 1466 of 1640 comparisons agree; 136 candidate-unknown, 38 value. All 38 value records are joint returns with no traditional contributions (classm.ira.2, classm.f5695.5, classm.f8960.2), several with person.plan supplied without a Schedule C. Of the 136 candidate-unknown records, 128 are no-contribution returns where spouse coverage is not asked and 8 need person.plan without a Schedule C (person.plan (the self-employed person’s own SEP or SIMPLE) is read by the project only with that person’s Schedule C (person.ira_se_plan, amb.2025.ira_covered); without a Schedule C the interview never asks it and the answer is necessarily none, since other self-employment (Schedules E and F, partnerships) is refused by scope.schedule1). On contributing returns the answers agree; on a return with no traditional IRA contributions the worksheet is not used and no amount reads the line. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 97: "If you checked “No” on line 1a (and “No” on line 1b if married filing jointly), skip lines 2 through 6, enter the applicable amount below on line 7a (and line 7b, if applicable), and go to line 8."; i1040gi p. 95, Line 20: "If you made contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025, you may be able to take an IRA deduction." Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/ira.json; 1,083 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 57 partial records): 93 of 1640 comparisons agree; 943 candidate-unknown, 517 value, 87 candidate-refuses. All 517 value records have no traditional contributions: the project shows zero and the candidate the applicable $7,000 or $8,000; line 12a is the smallest of line 7a, 10 and 11a, and 11a is zero, so no deduction differs. 926 of the 943 candidate-unknown records are no-contribution returns needing coverage or age; 17 contributing returns need person.plan without a Schedule C (person.plan (the self-employed person’s own SEP or SIMPLE) is read by the project only with that person’s Schedule C (person.ira_se_plan, amb.2025.ira_covered); without a Schedule C the interview never asks it and the answer is necessarily none, since other self-employment (Schedules E and F, partnerships) is refused by scope.schedule1). The 87 candidate-refuses records are returns the project refuses for other cited gates (scope). On contributing returns the two lines agree on every record, including the 35%/70% rates, the $10,000/$20,000 thresholds and the $200 floor. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 97: "If you checked “No” on line 1a (and “No” on line 1b if married filing jointly), skip lines 2 through 6, enter the applicable amount below on line 7a (and line 7b, if applicable), and go to line 8."; i1040gi p. 95, Line 20, item 6: "You must file a joint return to deduct contributions to your spouse’s IRA." On contributing returns the lines agree. Project stands.

Ruling: model error; p590a p. 6, What Is Compensation?, "Wages, salaries, tips, professional fees, bonuses, and other amounts you receive for providing personal services are compensation"; i1040gi p. 98, line 8, "Wages, salaries, tips, etc. Generally, this is the amount reported in box 1 of Form W-2". The reply takes line 1a only; household-employee wages (line 1b), tips not on a W-2 (line 1c) and Form 8919 wages (line 1g) are pay for services and compensation, and leaving them out refused a lawful contribution (BUG-1156, fixture ira.household_wages_comp). 'Generally' marks box 1 as the usual source, not the whole of the line. Where lines 1b, 1c and 1g are zero the two agree.

Ruling: ambiguity; p590a p. 7: "Self-employment loss. If you have a net loss from self-employment, don’t subtract the loss from your salaries or wages when figuring your total compensation." The project floors each spouse's self-employment earned income at zero before adding (amb.2025.ira_se_floor, owner decision); the candidate floors the combined total, the other recorded reading. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/ira.json; 1,083 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 57 partial records): 671 of 1640 comparisons agree; 921 candidate-unknown, 46 project-refuses, 2 value. The 2 value records are joint returns where one spouse has a Schedule C loss (generated 293: $157,316.78 against $109,209.37; generated 491), both refused for other gates. Of the 921 candidate-unknown records, 792 are returns without a Schedule C where the candidate's unconditional ira.se_capital screen asks a question whose answer is necessarily No (representation), and 129 have a Schedule C but no traditional contributions, where the source needs no such answer (model error in the candidate's screen). The 46 project-refuses records are Schedule C returns refused by cited Schedule C and plan screens (person.sc[].screened, s179.multi, person.plan_screened), scope. Project stands.

Ruling: model error. Triage .transcription/triage/2025/ira.json (log sha matches): 2,680/2,728 agree; 44 candidate-unknown, 4 value; completed: 16 candidate-unknown. As the landing-round ruling. The project screen is any(care_payments, deferred_comp, fellowship, reservist_repaid), as its label says ("deferred compensation, a fellowship not on a Form W-2, a reservist repayment, difficulty of care payments"). The reply drops ira.reservist_repaid (i1040gi p. 95 item 9, "Don’t include any repayments of qualified reservist distributions. You can’t deduct them") and folds in two cases the project handles on separate lines: the joint traditional-plus-Roth case of item 2 ("don’t use the IRA Deduction Worksheet in these instructions", the project's line at forms/2025/ira.yaml under item 2 reading ira.roth_total) and ira.se_capital (refused through ira.se_capital_gate on line 9). Differences are 44 candidate-unknowns (16 on completed returns: the reply reads ira.se_capital and the roth sums unasked) and 4 values, none on a completed return. The project line is right under the source.
